title: Instagram's API Rejected 40% of My Posts. Now Under 5% | vitalii.no
description:
Why Instagram silently refuses posts, and how measuring the picture before sending it cut the failure rate from 40 percent to under 5.

Instagram publishing was a constant battle. The API silently rejected posts for strict aspect ratio rules, anything outside 4:5 to 1.91:1, and for accounts that were not business accounts. Reels demanded a multi-step dance: create a media container, poll its status, then publish. And the errors that came back were bare numbers — #10, #24, #100, #190 — with no indication of what to fix. Two out of every five posts failed.

The post-to-instagram Supabase Edge Function, written in Deno, now orchestrates the whole flow. Aspect-ratio pre-validation parses the image binary headers locally to read its real dimensions and rejects invalid media before a single byte reaches Instagram. For Reels it creates the container and polls status every 10 seconds, up to 30 attempts, and only publishes once Instagram reports the media is ready. Every known error code is mapped to a plain, actionable fix instruction, and a caption formatter keeps posts inside the 2,200 character limit so nothing is silently truncated.

The failure rate fell from 40 percent to consistently under 5. More importantly, a failed post is now self-diagnosable: the error arrives with its fix attached, instead of sending me back into Facebook's documentation.
